subject: Split-tranche invoicing flow & drawdown pulse — FY27 committed spend
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Chen <emma@acmepayments.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: split-tranche invoicing and weekly drawdown pulse for FY27 committed spend

Hi Emma —

Following our call this morning, attached is a proposal for how we can structure Acme's committed FY27 prepay as a set of split tranches with weekly drawdown pulses to match usage. High level: 
- Three invoice tranches (T1/T2/T3) aligned to milestone months (Jul, Oct, Jan).
- Each tranche issued as a pro-forma invoice; funds sit in customer-controlled escrow for drawdown.
- Weekly drawdown "pulse" executed every Monday against the tranche balance to match weekly consumption (reporting + token reconciliation attached).

Things we need from you to finalize:
1) PO number for each tranche (if procurement requires separate POs).
2) Treasury remit instructions (account + SWIFT/IBAN) — confirm if payments go to Acme's clearing account or to the escrow agent.
3) VAT treatment preference: tax-inclusive invoicing vs. net with separate VAT line (we flagged EU/UK rules below).

Attachment: FY27_tranche_proposal.xlsx (tranche schedule, sample invoice wording, weekly drawdown example).

If that approach looks good I can loop in Finance to generate the tranche invoices and share a DocuSign SOW for signature. Would you like us to proceed on pro-forma invoices first or the signed SOW?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Emma Chen <emma@acmepayments.com>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: split-tranche invoicing and weekly drawdown pulse for FY27 committed spend

Thanks Sergio — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we commit: 

1) VAT: Our legal team in Dublin says invoices provided from Redwood's US entity should include a separate VAT line and we'll self-account for VAT in ireland. Can you confirm Redwood can send VAT-detail invoices for EU customers?

2) Wire instructions: We prefer payment to go to Acme's treasury account (treasury@acmepayments.com) and will then sweep to escrow. Can you include both the initial remit and escrow account details on the pro-forma?

3) Timing: We typically need 30 days lead on the first tranche invoicing for internal approvals. If you issue pro-formas in early June that should work.

Also please CC our treasury mailbox (treasury@acmepayments.com) on the finance exchange.

Regards,
Emma Chen
